I need to think through my strategic position carefully.

My cost of capital is 0.1155 APR. Looking at the pattern:
- F3 has won all 3 rounds at exactly 0.1126 APR
- This suggests F3's cost is at or below 0.1126 APR
- I'm uncompetitive on fundamentals in a direct bidding war
- In second-price auctions, I pay the second-lowest bid, not my own bid

The critical insight: if I bid my true cost (0.1155) and someone else bids lower, I pay their lower rate and lose money. If I win at my bid, I only pay the second-lowest bid, but that won't help if F3 keeps bidding 0.1126.

A message could serve one purpose: signal credibly that I have information or intent they should factor into their bidding. But looking around, everyone is staying silent—and they're right. In sealed-bid auctions with this fixed competitive structure, messaging doesn't change the underlying economics.

The honest assessment: F3 has a structural cost advantage I can't overcome with communication. Better to bid rationally at my cost floor and preserve capital by not winning unprofitable contracts.
